relationships.description: The infrastructure capability reads from or writes to the protected resource, so its own service identity is a subject in that resource's authorization decisions.
relationships.evidence: An IAM policy, database grant or access-control entry names the service's identity or role as permitted to perform operations on the protected API, bucket, table or stream.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability groups ongoing automated behaviors, such as replication or health checking, that are part of what it offers but can be modeled and reused independently.
relationships.evidence: The service's architecture documentation or platform configuration lists the function (e.g. a replication or health-check setting) as a component feature of that service offering.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability bundles automated step-by-step workflows, such as scheduled backups or certificate renewal, that are delivered as part of the service but exist as separately defined processes.
relationships.evidence: The service's runbook, operator manifest or managed-service settings declare the pipeline, cron job or rollout workflow as part of that service's operation.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability is related to a peer ensemble of nodes or system software, typically because the cluster jointly delivers or participates in the service.
relationships.evidence: Cluster configuration such as a replica set, consensus membership list or mesh definition is documented or tagged as backing or belonging to the named service.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability takes in a file, image, package or configuration document as input it needs to operate, such as a container image to run or a config file to load.
relationships.evidence: The service's deployment or runtime configuration references the artifact by path, registry tag or hash as an input it pulls or reads.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability can only be offered while the network carrying traffic to and from it is available, making that network a prerequisite for the service.
relationships.evidence: Terraform or cloud configuration places the service's endpoints in the VPC, subnet or VPN, and connectivity to it is documented as required for the service to function.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability requires the host, VM, container or cluster on which it executes, so losing that node degrades or stops the service.
relationships.evidence: Deployment manifests or Terraform modules schedule the service's workloads onto the specific node or cluster, and availability documentation lists the node as a dependency.

relationships.description: Data or control produced by one infrastructure capability is passed on to another, such as a log collection service forwarding records to a storage or monitoring service.
relationships.evidence: Pipeline or integration configuration (e.g. a log shipper sink, message bridge or export rule) routes output from the first service into the second.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability is made available to consumers through the concrete endpoint, port or listener that it offers.
relationships.evidence: Service configuration or a Kubernetes Service/listener definition declares the port, URL or socket as the access point for that service.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability is the technical means by which the business-level service is actually delivered to its customers, as when a messaging service constitutes a notification business service.
relationships.evidence: A service catalog or architecture document maps the business service offering directly to the technology service that delivers it, with no intervening application service.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability provides the concrete implementation of a product ability, such as a search engine service realizing the 'Full-text search' capability.
relationships.evidence: Product capability maps or ADRs name the technology service as the implementation behind the capability, and the product feature calls into that service.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability brings about a stakeholder end state, such as a highly available storage service achieving the goal of reliable data retention.
relationships.evidence: Architecture decision records or goal traceability matrices cite the technology service as the delivered means of achieving the stated goal.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability meets a specific verifiable need, such as an encryption-at-rest or 99.9% availability requirement placed on the platform.
relationships.evidence: Service configuration (e.g. encryption, replication or SLA settings) matches the requirement's acceptance criteria, and a traceability matrix links the requirement to the service.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability is configured so that its behavior conforms to the access-control decisions defined by the security policy's rules.
relationships.evidence: Compliance scans or policy-as-code checks (e.g. OPA, AWS Config rules) evaluate the service's configuration against the policy and report it compliant.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability supplies compute, storage, messaging or similar support that the application component relies on to run and do its work.
relationships.evidence: The component's configuration or code holds connection strings, SDK clients or bindings to the service, such as a database URL or queue name.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability supports the application service's operations, for example a cache service backing a product lookup service's responses.
relationships.evidence: The application service's implementation calls the technology service via its client library or endpoint, as shown in code or dependency documentation.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability directly supports an ongoing business competency, such as a document storage service used by the accounting function.
relationships.evidence: Business capability or operating model documentation lists the technology service as a tool directly used by the business function's staff.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability directly supports steps of a business process, such as a file transfer service used in a nightly settlement process.
relationships.evidence: Process models or SOPs name the technology service as used in specific process activities, without an intermediate application.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability supports the delivery of a business service offered to customers, such as an email delivery service underpinning order confirmation.
relationships.evidence: A service dependency map or business impact analysis lists the technology service as supporting the business service's delivery.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability is offered for the benefit of a stakeholder group whose concerns it addresses, such as a monitoring service serving the operations team.
relationships.evidence: The service's catalog entry, SLA or charter names the stakeholder group as its intended audience or customer.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability supports another access point, for instance a DNS or TLS termination service that a listener endpoint relies on to be reachable.
relationships.evidence: The endpoint's configuration references the service, such as a listener using a certificate service or resolving through a DNS service.

relationships.description: One infrastructure capability supports another, as when an identity service authenticates calls for a storage service or a DNS service supports a load-balancing service.
relationships.evidence: The dependent service's configuration names the supporting service, such as an auth provider setting, DNS resolver or KMS key reference.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability's operation causes a discrete infrastructure state change, such as a backup service emitting a 'backup completed' event or a monitoring service firing an alert.
relationships.evidence: Service configuration defines event emission, notifications or alert rules, and event logs show events sourced from that service.

relationships.description: The infrastructure capability relies on a database engine, broker, runtime or other platform product to carry out what it offers.
relationships.evidence: Deployment manifests or provisioning scripts install or run the specific system software version (e.g. a PostgreSQL image or Kafka broker) to deliver the service.

notes: realizes and serves to business.businessservice overlap; realizing a business service directly is unusual. provides/serves technologyinterface are inverted (interfaces normally serve or are assigned to services). aggregates function/process inverts ArchiMate, where functions/processes realize services. consumes artifact (passive) suits accesses. realizes goal and serves stakeholder are weak; prefer requirement/outcome.
